name: Ubuntu
comment: A popular Linux distribution based on Debian, known for its ease of use and strong community support.

name: Fedora
comment: A cutting-edge Linux distribution sponsored by Red Hat, known for its focus on innovation and open-source software.

name: Arch Linux
comment: A lightweight and flexible Linux distribution that follows a rolling release model, allowing users to customize their system.

name: Debian
comment: One of the oldest and most stable Linux distributions, serving as the base for many other distros including Ubuntu.

name: Linux Mint
comment: A beginner-friendly distribution based on Ubuntu/Debian, offering a familiar desktop experience with Cinnamon, MATE, or Xfce.

name: openSUSE
comment: A community distribution sponsored by SUSE, offering both a stable release (Leap) and a rolling release (Tumbleweed).

name: Manjaro
comment: An Arch-based distribution that offers the power of Arch with a more user-friendly installer and curated packages.

name: Pop!_OS
comment: Developed by System76, an Ubuntu-based distro tailored for developers and gamers with strong GPU support.

name: elementary OS
comment: A design-focused Ubuntu-based distribution with its own Pantheon desktop, aiming for a macOS-like experience.

name: Zorin OS
comment: An Ubuntu-based distro designed to ease the transition for Windows and macOS users with familiar layouts.

name: MX Linux
comment: A Debian-based distribution combining elegant desktops with simple configuration and solid stability.

name: Solus
comment: An independently built rolling-release distribution featuring its own Budgie desktop environment.

name: Void Linux
comment: An independent rolling-release distribution using the runit init system instead of systemd.

name: NixOS
comment: A unique distribution built on the Nix package manager, enabling fully reproducible and declarative system configurations.

name: Alpine Linux
comment: A security-oriented, lightweight distribution built with musl libc and BusyBox, popular for containers.

name: Gentoo
comment: A source-based distribution where packages are compiled from source, giving deep control over optimization.

name: Slackware
comment: The oldest surviving Linux distribution, valued for its simplicity and Unix-like philosophy.

name: CentOS Stream
comment: A rolling-release distribution that sits upstream of Red Hat Enterprise Linux, used for testing future RHEL features.

name: Rocky Linux
comment: A community-driven, enterprise-grade distribution built to be bug-for-bug compatible with RHEL.

name: AlmaLinux
comment: An open-source, RHEL-compatible distribution created after CentOS shifted to a rolling model.

name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
comment: A commercial, enterprise-focused distribution known for stability, long-term support, and certification.

name: SUSE Linux Enterprise
comment: A commercial enterprise distribution from SUSE, widely used in business and mainframe environments.

name: Oracle Linux
comment: A RHEL-compatible enterprise distribution from Oracle, offering an interchangeable kernel option (UEK).

name: Kali Linux
comment: A Debian-based distribution preloaded with tools for penetration testing and security auditing.

name: Parrot OS
comment: A security and privacy-focused distribution aimed at pentesting, forensics, and anonymous browsing.

name: BlackArch Linux
comment: An Arch-based penetration testing distribution with a huge repository of security tools.

name: Tails
comment: A live, amnesic distribution that routes all traffic through Tor to preserve privacy and anonymity.

name: Qubes OS
comment: A security-focused distribution that isolates applications into separate virtual machines (qubes).

name: Whonix
comment: A privacy-focused distribution split into a Gateway and Workstation VM, routing all traffic through Tor.

name: Deepin
comment: A Chinese-developed distribution known for its polished, custom Deepin Desktop Environment (DDE).

name: EndeavourOS
comment: A near-vanilla, Arch-based distribution designed to be simple to install while staying close to Arch itself.

name: Garuda Linux
comment: An Arch-based distribution with performance tweaks, BTRFS snapshots, and a striking default aesthetic.

name: CachyOS
comment: A performance-oriented Arch-based distribution using optimized kernels and packages for speed.

name: Artix Linux
comment: An Arch-based distribution that replaces systemd with alternative init systems like OpenRC or runit.

name: Puppy Linux
comment: An extremely lightweight distribution designed to run entirely in RAM, ideal for old hardware.

name: antiX
comment: A lightweight, systemd-free Debian-based distribution for older and low-resource computers.

name: Devuan
comment: A fork of Debian created specifically to offer an init-system-agnostic alternative without systemd.

name: PCLinuxOS
comment: An independent, rolling-release distribution focused on ease of use with a KDE-centric desktop.

name: Mageia
comment: A community fork of Mandriva Linux focused on stability and a user-friendly configuration toolset.

name: Raspberry Pi OS
comment: A Debian-based distribution optimized for Raspberry Pi single-board computers.

name: Kubuntu
comment: An official Ubuntu flavor that ships the KDE Plasma desktop environment by default.

name: Xubuntu
comment: An official Ubuntu flavor using the lightweight Xfce desktop environment.

name: Lubuntu
comment: An official Ubuntu flavor built around the lightweight LXQt desktop for older hardware.

name: Ubuntu MATE
comment: An official Ubuntu flavor featuring the traditional MATE desktop environment.

name: Ubuntu Studio
comment: An official Ubuntu flavor tailored for multimedia creation, with audio, video, and graphics tools preinstalled.

name: KDE neon
comment: An Ubuntu-based distribution maintained by the KDE community to showcase the very latest Plasma releases.

name: Bodhi Linux
comment: A lightweight Ubuntu-based distribution built around the Moksha desktop, a fork of Enlightenment.

name: Peppermint OS
comment: A lightweight, cloud-focused Debian-based distribution combining local apps with web app integration.

name: TinyCore Linux
comment: A minimalist distribution just a few megabytes in size, built to run fully in RAM.

name: SteamOS
comment: Valve's Arch-based distribution optimized for gaming, powering the Steam Deck.

name: Bazzite
comment: An immutable, Fedora-based gaming distribution built on the same tech as SteamOS, usable on any PC.

name: Nobara
comment: A Fedora-based distribution created by a Valve contributor, tuned for gaming and content creation.

name: Amog-OS
comment: A Linux distribution themed around the popular game 'Among Us', featuring custom wallpapers, icons, and a unique desktop environment.

name: FreeBSD
comment: A powerful BSD operating system known for its performance, security, and clean UNIX heritage.

name: OpenBSD
comment: A security-focused BSD operating system celebrated for its proactive code auditing and strong defaults.

name: NetBSD
comment: A portable BSD system built to run on many different architectures, from embedded devices to servers.

name: DragonFly BSD
comment: A BSD variant focused on performance, SMP scalability, and a modern kernel architecture.

name: GhostBSD
comment: A desktop-centric BSD distribution built around MATE and designed for ease of use.

name: MidnightBSD
comment: A desktop-oriented BSD distribution focused on polishing the user experience for everyday systems.

name: TrueNAS Scale
comment: A Debian-based NAS platform with a BSD-inspired storage stack and enterprise-grade features.

name: BoredOS
comment:
A niche, experimental hobby operating system written in C and x86-64 assembly.
Fun fact, I made this wallpaper and it ships with the OS.

name: TempleOS
comment: A unique, biblical-themed operating system created by Terry A. Davis, known for its simplicity and 16-bit color graphics.

name: Red Star OS
comment: A North Korean Linux-based operating system with a heavily modified KDE desktop and unique features. Fun fact, I managed to install it and change the language to English, but im yet to get the internet working on it.

name: Astra Linux
comment: A Russian Linux distribution designed for government and military use, with enhanced security features.

name: Gendbuntu
comment: A custom version of the Ubuntu Linux operating system created and used by the French National Gendarmerie (Military Police).

name: The Bleed Kernel
comment: The Bleed Kernel is a Multitasking Monolithic Operating System Kernel for x86_64 Machines.
